chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Adami, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Zayyat, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'I pronounced zihar from my wife.' He said to me: 'How did you say it?' I said: 'You are upon me like the back of my mother, if I do such and such.' He said to me: 'There is no penalty upon you, and do not repeat it.'

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (Imam Ali al-Rida, the 8th Imam)
key_terms.ظَهَرْتُ: I pronounced zihar (a form of pre-Islamic/Islamic divorce where a husband declares his wife unlawful to him by comparing her back to his mother's back)
key_terms.كَظَهْرِ أُمِّي: Like the back of my mother (the standard formula for zihar)
key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْكَ: There is no penalty/expitation upon you

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zihar when the phrase is used conditionally?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the conditionality of zihar, establishing that a conditional declaration ('if I do X') does not trigger the immediate expiation (kaffarah) required for an effective zihar. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise linguistic formulation in marital jurisprudence, distinguishing between the act of pronouncement and the binding legal consequence. The instruction 'do not repeat' underscores the preventative nature of this ruling to avoid unnecessary financial or ritual burdens.
